subject: history_social
passage: At Kalibangan, an archaeological site in the Indian state of Rajasthan, researchers uncovered one of the oldest plowed fields ever found. The field dates to about 2800 BCE. Its furrows were cut in two directions, crossing one another to form a grid. Farmers in the same region still plow some fields in this crisscross way today, so that they can grow two different crops in a single field.
stem: According to the text, what is notable about the furrows in the ancient field at Kalibangan?

choices.A: They were cut with a kind of plow that was later forgotten in the region.
choices.B: They are deeper than the furrows found at any other ancient site.
choices.C: They cross one another in a pattern that farmers in the region still use.
choices.D: They show that early farmers there grew only one crop in each field.

explanation.why: The text says the furrows were cut "in two directions, crossing one another to form a grid," and that farmers in the same region "still plow some fields in this crisscross way today." The correct choice restates both of these details.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The text says the crisscross method is still used today, not that it was forgotten.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The text never compares the depth of these furrows with others.
explanation.C: Correct. The furrows form a crisscross grid, and the text says local farmers still plow some fields this way.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The text links the crisscross pattern to growing two crops in a single field, not one.
